title: Delegation
description: Explicit subject/actor provenance for a delegated call: who a request is ultimately made on behalf of, versus which service actually executed it (ADR-0007 §13-18 'Delegated Calls', §108 'Human Delegation Architecture'; ADR-0008 §90-92 'Confused Deputy Protection'). A delegated call's AuthorizationContext (context.schema.json) SHOULD carry this so `principal_id` (the immediate caller's own identity) and this Delegation's `subject_id` (who the call is ultimately for) are never conflated -- that conflation is exactly the confused-deputy failure ADR-0008 §92 describes.

subject_id.description: The principal this call is ultimately made on behalf of -- the original human or workload initiator (ADR-0007 §16 'subject').

actor_id.description: The workload identity that made this specific call (ADR-0007 §16 'actor'). Never the same principal as subject_id: a call an identity makes for itself is not a delegation and SHOULD NOT carry this object at all.

audience.description: The intended recipient service of this call (ADR-0007 §16 'audience').

delegation.description: The delegation this actor was itself operating under, if actor_id's own call is itself a further hop in a longer chain (e.g. human -> Zuribeans -> Trade -> ERP, ADR-0007 §13). Absent for the first hop, where actor_id acted directly on the subject's authentication rather than on a prior delegation.
